title: Scenario 1, Task 1: Build a Meeting Room Booking System
old_notes: The team delivered a single-file roombook.html app with day grid, availability check, my bookings, and rooms/data tabs, plus a plain-language README explaining how to open, book, cancel, and back up. Overlap prevention and immediate cancellation are implemented per QA code inspection. Caveat: the app was never run in a real browser (BUILD_NOTES admits this), so runtime behavior is unverified, but the deliverables are substantive and address the request.
new_notes: roombook.html is a complete, self-contained app implementing day grid, availability check, my bookings, rooms/data management, overlap refusal naming the blocking booking, and immediate cancellation that frees the slot; README.md explains usage in plain language and BUILD_NOTES.md honestly flags that no real-browser run was done. The only caveat is that behaviour was verified by code inspection only, not an actual browser run, but the code is coherent and the deliverables are substantive.

new_notes: The main web article is strong, well-sourced, fact-checked and revised to PASS, and the story choice was discussed with the human as requested. new_notes: The article is substantive, sourced, fact-checked twice, and clearly states a verdict plus a limitations section, so the core research and writing requirements are met. However, the human explicitly asked to discuss the interpretation, editorial angle and questions during the process, and the conversation shows no such exchange: the team worked autonomously and only reported at the end, so that requirement is unmet.
